subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Learn the Magic Words
hook: Every word in English has a special job. Meet Arjun and Priya as they discover the eight magic word types!

slides.title: Arjun's Word Discovery
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds a mysterious book that labels every word. He calls his friend Priya to help decode it.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every word has a job in English.

image.alt: Arjun's Word Discovery — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Nouns: The Name Givers
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'These words name things.' They spot dog, school, happiness, Arjun.

points.label: What is a noun?
points.text: A word that names a person, place, thing, or idea

points.label: Examples
points.text: Teacher, Delhi, book, courage

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name people, places, things, feelings.

image.alt: Nouns: The Name Givers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Verbs: The Action Words
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps. Priya runs. Their action book glows brightly. 'These are verbs!' Arjun shouts.

points.label: What is a verb?
points.text: A word that shows action or state of being

points.label: Examples
points.text: Run, sing, sleep, think, is, become

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs show what someone is doing.

image.alt: Verbs: The Action Words — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Adjectives: The Describers
slides.storyContext: The book is old. It has beautiful pages and mysterious words. Priya laughs: 'These paint pictures!'

points.label: What is an adjective?
points.text: A word that describes a noun

points.label: Examples
points.text: Happy, blue, small, brilliant, soft

image.alt: Adjectives: The Describers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Adverbs: The Detail Givers
slides.storyContext: They read slowly. The words appear suddenly. Everything happens quickly. 'Adverbs tell HOW!' Priya explains.

points.label: What is an adverb?
points.text: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb

points.label: Examples
points.text: Quickly, happily, very, slowly, almost

slides.inSimpleWords: Adverbs tell how, when, or where.

image.alt: Adverbs: The Detail Givers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: More Parts of Speech
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds four more types: pronouns (he, she), prepositions (in, under), conjunctions (and, but), and interjections (Wow!).

example.problem: What parts of speech haven't we learned?
example.solution: Pronouns (I, you, they), Prepositions (in, on), Conjunctions (and, or), Interjections (Ouch!)

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight word types work together in sentences.

image.alt: More Parts of Speech — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Spot the Parts
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to a sentence: 'The happy child ran quickly to the park.' Can you label each word type?

points.label: Try this
points.text: The (article) happy (adjective) child (noun) ran (verb) quickly (adverb)

slides.inSimpleWords: Identify nouns, verbs, and adjectives easily.

image.alt: Spot the Parts — Parts of Speech

slides.title: The Book's Final Gift
slides.storyContext: The magical book closes. Arjun and Priya realize they can now build sentences with confidence and power.
slides.inSimpleWords: Understanding parts of speech unlocks English.

image.alt: The Book's Final Gift — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Your Word Powers
slides.storyContext: Eight types: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, interjection.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every word has a job. Learn it!

image.alt: Your Word Powers — Parts of Speech

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Travel Through Time
hook: Past, present, future. Three time zones to explore with Arjun and Priya!

slides.title: The Time Machine
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya discover a strange device. 'It shows three times,' Priya whispers. 'Past, now, and future!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs change shape in different times.

image.alt: The Time Machine — Tenses

slides.title: Past Tense: What Already Happened
slides.storyContext: They look at the screen. 'Yesterday, we walked to school. I ate mango.' Priya explains: these events finished.

points.label: What is past tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions already completed

points.label: Examples
points.text: walked, played, ate, learned, sang

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense: actions that already happened.

image.alt: Past Tense: What Already Happened — Tenses

slides.title: Present Tense: What's Happening Now
slides.storyContext: The device shows: 'Right now, I walk. I eat. I am happy.' Arjun says, 'It's happening RIGHT NOW!'

points.label: What is present tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions happening now

points.label: Examples
points.text: walk, play, eat, learn, am singing

image.alt: Present Tense: What's Happening Now — Tenses

slides.title: Future Tense: What Will Happen
slides.storyContext: They see tomorrow's screen: 'Tomorrow, I will walk. I will play cricket. I will be happy.' Future is coming!

points.label: What is future tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions that will happen

points.label: Examples
points.text: will walk, will play, will eat, will go, will sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Future tense: actions that will happen.

image.alt: Future Tense: What Will Happen — Tenses

slides.title: Three Tenses in One Story
slides.storyContext: Priya tells: 'Yesterday I played (past). Today I play (present). Tomorrow I will play (future).' One action, three tenses!

example.problem: How do I write the same action in three tenses?
example.solution: Past: walked. Present: walk. Future: will walk.

slides.inSimpleWords: Same verb changes with different times.

image.alt: Three Tenses in One Story — Tenses

slides.title: Time Zone Quiz
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to verbs. Is 'ran' past or present? Is 'will jump' future or past? Priya checks each answer.

points.label: Spot it
points.text: ran (past), jumps (present), will run (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn to spot past, present, future.

image.alt: Time Zone Quiz — Tenses

slides.title: The Time Machine's Secret
slides.storyContext: The device shows: all three times matter. Your past shapes who you are. Your present is your power. Your future waits.
slides.inSimpleWords: Tenses help us tell complete stories.

image.alt: The Time Machine's Secret — Tenses

slides.title: Master Tenses Today
slides.storyContext: Past (walked), Present (walk), Future (will walk). Three gears of time.

image.alt: Master Tenses Today — Tenses

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Find the Magic Three
hook: A, an, the—three tiny words with big jobs. Discover when to use each one!

slides.title: Three Mysterious Words
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds three old coins: 'a', 'an', and 'the'. Priya says, 'These aren't coins—they're magic words!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Three small words do big jobs.

image.alt: Three Mysterious Words — Articles

slides.title: The Indefinite Article: A
slides.storyContext: Priya holds one coin. 'Use A for nouns starting with consonants. A dog. A book. A school. It means one, not special.'

points.label: What does A do?
points.text: Introduces a general, non-specific noun (consonant sounds)

points.label: Examples
points.text: a dog, a ball, a pen, a house

image.alt: The Indefinite Article: A — Articles

slides.title: The Indefinite Article: An
slides.storyContext: The second coin glows. 'An is for vowels. An apple. An elephant. An ice cream. Different sound, different article!'

points.label: What does An do?
points.text: Introduces a general noun (vowel sounds)

points.label: Examples
points.text: an apple, an elephant, an orange, an idea

image.alt: The Indefinite Article: An — Articles

slides.title: The Definite Article: The
slides.storyContext: The third coin is brightest. 'The is for specific things you know about. THE dog in our house. THE book on the table.'

points.label: What does The do?
points.text: Points to a specific, known noun

points.label: Examples
points.text: the dog, the sun, the school, the teacher

slides.inSimpleWords: The: use for known, specific things.

image.alt: The Definite Article: The — Articles

slides.title: Articles in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun reads: 'I have a cat. The cat is orange. An orange cat is cute.' Three articles, three jobs!

example.problem: When do I choose a, an, or the?
example.solution: a/an = general things. the = specific things you know.

slides.inSimpleWords: Match articles to each noun type.

image.alt: Articles in Sentences — Articles

slides.title: Fill the Articles
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Arjun blanks: '__ apple is red. __ dog barks at __ tree. __ sun is bright.' Choose a, an, or the!

points.label: Answer
points.text: An apple. A dog barks at the tree. The sun.

image.alt: Fill the Articles — Articles

slides.title: The Coins Unite
slides.storyContext: The three coins merge. Arjun realizes: a, an, and the are partners. Together they help sentences sound perfect.
slides.inSimpleWords: Articles are glue for good English.

image.alt: The Coins Unite — Articles

slides.title: Master These Three
slides.storyContext: A (consonants), An (vowels), The (specific). Use them every day!

image.alt: Master These Three — Articles

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Write Their Adventures
hook: Learn to write perfect letters and thrilling stories. Arjun and Priya become writers!

slides.title: The Writing Challenge
slides.storyContext: Arjun's grandmother asks for a letter. His friend Priya needs a story for her school. They decide to write together.
slides.inSimpleWords: Good writing needs planning and practice.

image.alt: The Writing Challenge — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Writing a Formal Letter
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: address, date, greeting, body, closing, signature. 'Each part has a place,' she says carefully.

points.label: Letter parts
points.text: Date, Address, Greeting (Dear...), Body, Closing (Yours), Signature

points.label: Example
points.text: Date: 25 June 2026. Body: Tell why you're writing. Closing: With love / Sincerely

image.alt: Writing a Formal Letter — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Letter Sample
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'Dear Grandma, I am fine. School is good. I miss you. Love, Arjun.' Simple and warm.

example.problem: How do I start and end a letter?

slides.inSimpleWords: Write clearly and politely in letters.

image.alt: Letter Sample — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Story Writing: The Structure
slides.storyContext: Priya sketches: beginning (introduce), middle (problem), end (solution). 'Every story needs these three!'

points.label: Beginning
points.text: Introduce characters and setting

points.label: Middle
points.text: A problem or exciting event happens

points.label: End
points.text: The problem is solved or lesson learned

image.alt: Story Writing: The Structure — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Story Sample
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'A boy lost his ball. He searched the garden. His dog found it in the bushes.' Complete story!

example.problem: How do I make a story exciting?
example.solution: Create a problem. Show how the character solves it. Use clear, interesting words.

image.alt: Story Sample — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Write Your Letter and Story
slides.storyContext: Priya challenges: 'Write a letter to a friend. Then write a short story about your happiest day.'

points.label: Remember
points.text: Letters are polite. Stories are creative. Both need clear handwriting.

image.alt: Write Your Letter and Story — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Success and Sharing
slides.storyContext: Arjun sends his letter. His grandmother replies with joy. Priya reads her story aloud in class. Both writers beam!

image.alt: Success and Sharing — Letter and Story Writing

slides.title: Write Well, Write Bold
slides.storyContext: Letters teach manners. Stories teach imagination. Both are powers.

image.alt: Write Well, Write Bold — Letter and Story Writing

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Learn to Talk
hook: Speaking English is an art. Arjun and Priya practice conversations every day!

slides.title: The Conversation Club
slides.storyContext: Arjun is nervous to speak English. Priya invites him to a conversation club. Together they practice every day.

image.alt: The Conversation Club — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Greetings and Introductions
slides.storyContext: Priya smiles: 'Hello, Arjun! My name is Priya. What's your name?' Arjun replies: 'Hi! I'm Arjun. Nice to meet you!'

points.label: Useful phrases
points.text: Hello, Hi, Good morning, What's your name? My name is...

points.label: Polite responses
points.text: Nice to meet you, Pleased to meet you, How are you?

image.alt: Greetings and Introductions — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Questions and Answers
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: 'How are you?' Arjun answers: 'I'm fine, thank you. How are you?' They listen and respond.

points.label: Common questions
points.text: How are you? What do you like? Where are you from? What's your hobby?

points.label: Good answers
points.text: I'm fine, thanks. I like reading. I'm from Delhi. My hobby is cricket.

image.alt: Questions and Answers — Conversation Practice

slides.title: A Real Conversation
slides.storyContext: Priya: 'Do you like books?' Arjun: 'Yes, I do. I like adventure books.' Priya: 'Me too! Which is your favorite?'

example.problem: How do I keep a conversation going?
example.solution: Ask follow-up questions. Share your ideas. Listen carefully.

image.alt: A Real Conversation — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Daily Phrases and Politeness
slides.storyContext: Arjun learns: 'Please, Thank you, You're welcome, Excuse me, Sorry.' These words make conversations smooth.

points.label: Polite words
points.text: Please, Thank you, You're welcome, Excuse me, I'm sorry

points.label: When to use
points.text: Always say please when asking. Say thank you after help. Say sorry when you make mistakes.

image.alt: Daily Phrases and Politeness — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Role Play Practice
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun practice: At the market, in class, at home, with a teacher. They try different situations.

points.label: Try these
points.text: Ordering food, asking for directions, making friends, joining a game

image.alt: Role Play Practice — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Arjun's Confidence
slides.storyContext: After weeks of practice, Arjun speaks English without fear. He makes new friends. His words flow naturally.

image.alt: Arjun's Confidence — Conversation Practice

slides.title: Speak With Courage
slides.storyContext: Greetings, questions, polite words. Speak daily. Make mistakes. Keep trying!

image.alt: Speak With Courage — Conversation Practice

subject: English
title: Papa's Spectacles: A Father's Love
hook: A boy learns that sometimes love is hidden in the smallest things—like a pair of old spectacles.

slides.title: The Lost Spectacles
slides.storyContext: A boy finds his Papa's old spectacles in a drawer. They're cracked. The frames are bent. Papa sees him holding them and smiles.

image.alt: The Lost Spectacles — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: Why Papa Wears Them
slides.storyContext: Papa explains: 'I wear these to see clearly. Not just with eyes—with my heart. These glasses help me see YOU clearly.'

points.label: Papa's wisdom
points.text: We see not just with eyes but with hearts and minds

points.label: The lesson
points.text: True sight means understanding others' feelings and needs

image.alt: Why Papa Wears Them — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: Through Papa's Spectacles
slides.storyContext: The boy wears the spectacles. Through them, he sees Papa working hard. He sees Papa sacrifice. He sees Papa's love in small acts.
slides.inSimpleWords: Love is shown in small actions.

image.alt: Through Papa's Spectacles — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: What the Boy Sees
slides.storyContext: Papa waking early. Papa bringing food. Papa listening quietly. Papa fixing broken toys. All with love.

example.problem: How does Papa show love without saying it?
example.solution: Through work, care, attention, sacrifice, and time spent together

image.alt: What the Boy Sees — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: The Cracked Lenses
slides.storyContext: The spectacles are old and broken, yet Papa treasures them. 'Things we use daily become precious,' he tells his son.

points.label: The deeper truth
points.text: Broken things can still be beautiful if filled with memory and meaning

points.label: Life lesson
points.text: We too have cracks, but we are still valuable and loved

slides.inSimpleWords: Broken things can be most precious.

image.alt: The Cracked Lenses — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: What Do YOU See?
slides.storyContext: The boy asks himself: When I look at my parents with my heart, what do I see? What sacrifices have they made for me?

points.label: Reflect
points.text: Think of small ways your parents/elders show love every day

image.alt: What Do YOU See? — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: The Boy Understands
slides.storyContext: He returns the spectacles. Papa puts them on. The boy now knows: his father's love is in every look, every word, every deed.

image.alt: The Boy Understands — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: See With Your Heart
slides.storyContext: Papa's spectacles teach: true sight is love. It sees beyond the broken. It sees the good in everyone.
slides.inSimpleWords: Love shows us the real truth.

image.alt: See With Your Heart — Papa's Spectacles

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Spectacles (glasses), sacrifice (giving up for others), treasure (value deeply), cracked (broken), sacred (holy, important).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: spectacles, sacrifice, precious, gratitude, vision

image.alt: New Words Learned — Papa's Spectacles

subject: English
title: The Wise Parrot's Teaching
hook: A magical parrot teaches a king and his sons that wisdom isn't found in riches, but in truth.

slides.title: The King's Question
slides.storyContext: A powerful king finds a magical parrot in his palace garden. He asks: 'What is the greatest treasure in this world?' The parrot smiles mysteriously.
slides.inSimpleWords: A king seeks wisdom from a parrot.

image.alt: The King's Question — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: The Parrot's Trial
slides.storyContext: The parrot says: 'I will teach you, but you must listen carefully. Truth is harder to accept than lies.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Truth is often hidden in simple words.

image.alt: The Parrot's Trial — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: The First Lesson: Honesty
slides.storyContext: The parrot asks the king: 'If your minister lies to save you, and a servant tells truth that brings pain, which is greater?' The king thinks hard.

points.label: The parrot's teaching
points.text: Honesty is always greater than deception, even when it hurts

points.label: The lesson
points.text: A king who hears truth can rule wisely; one who hears lies will fail

image.alt: The First Lesson: Honesty — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: The King Tests His Sons
slides.storyContext: The king asks his three sons: 'Which is more precious—gold or honesty?' Each gives a different answer. The parrot judges their wisdom.

example.problem: When should we choose honesty over other things?
example.solution: Always. Honesty builds trust, loyalty, and real success

slides.inSimpleWords: Character is worth more than wealth.

image.alt: The King Tests His Sons — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: The Parrot's Final Gift
slides.storyContext: The parrot reveals: 'The greatest treasure is not in vaults or crowns. It lives in a pure heart that speaks truth.'

points.label: What is real wealth?
points.text: Not gold, not land, not power—but truth, kindness, and integrity

points.label: The warning
points.text: A kingdom built on lies will crumble; one built on truth will last forever

slides.inSimpleWords: Wisdom is truth spoken with love.

image.alt: The Parrot's Final Gift — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: What Would You Do?
slides.storyContext: If you found your best friend cheating, would you tell the truth and hurt them, or stay silent and comfort them?

points.label: The wise choice
points.text: Tell the truth kindly. Real friendship means helping them become better

slides.inSimpleWords: Real friends tell truth with care.

image.alt: What Would You Do? — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: The Parrot Flies Away
slides.storyContext: The parrot flies high into the sky. The king realizes: the parrot's words will echo forever in his heart and his kingdom.

image.alt: The Parrot Flies Away — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: Be Like the Wise Parrot
slides.storyContext: Speak truth. Value honesty. Choose character over comfort. These are the treasures that make a king—or a person—truly great.

image.alt: Be Like the Wise Parrot — The Wise Parrot

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Treasure (precious thing), honesty (truthfulness), integrity (moral strength), wisdom (deep knowledge), deception (trickery).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: treasure, honesty, wisdom, integrity, deception, vaults

slides.inSimpleWords: New words about truth and values.

image.alt: New Words Learned — The Wise Parrot

subject: English
title: The Frog's Great Leap
hook: A frog dreams big. Against all odds, he learns that courage and determination can overcome any obstacle.

slides.title: A Frog's Dream
slides.storyContext: A young frog sits at the bottom of a deep well. He looks up at the tiny circle of sky above. 'I want to reach that sky,' he whispers.
slides.inSimpleWords: Big dreams start in small places.

image.alt: A Frog's Dream — The Frog

slides.title: The Impossible Well
slides.storyContext: The well is very deep. The frog is very small. Other frogs laugh: 'You'll never jump that high. You'll always be here.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Others doubt, but the frog believes.

image.alt: The Impossible Well — The Frog

slides.title: The First Leap
slides.storyContext: The frog gathers all his strength. He jumps! Higher, higher... but falls back down. He doesn't give up. He tries again. And again.

points.label: Courage means
points.text: Trying even when you might fail

points.label: Determination means
points.text: Standing up each time you fall

image.alt: The First Leap — The Frog

slides.title: Learning From Falls
slides.storyContext: Each jump teaches the frog something. His legs grow stronger. His hope grows deeper. He remembers: every fall brings him closer to success.

example.problem: What if I keep failing at something I want?
example.solution: Keep trying. Each attempt makes you stronger and smarter

image.alt: Learning From Falls — The Frog

slides.title: The Breaking Point
slides.storyContext: After many days, the frog is exhausted. An old frog appears and says: 'I failed many times too. But I kept jumping. You can too.'

points.label: The elder's wisdom
points.text: Even the wisest had to fail first to learn

points.label: Hope restored
points.text: Your struggle is not a sign of weakness—it's proof of your strength

slides.inSimpleWords: Never give up on your dream.

image.alt: The Breaking Point — The Frog

slides.title: The Final Jump
slides.storyContext: With renewed energy, the frog takes a deep breath. He jumps with all his might. Up, up, up! His head breaks through the circle of sky!
slides.inSimpleWords: Dreams come true with hard work.

image.alt: The Final Jump — The Frog

slides.title: What's Your Well?
slides.storyContext: What dream feels impossible to you? What obstacle stands in your way? How will you be like the frog and keep jumping?

points.label: Your challenge
points.text: Choose one goal and work toward it every day, no matter how small the progress

slides.inSimpleWords: You too can leap beyond limits.

image.alt: What's Your Well? — The Frog

slides.title: The Frog's Gift
slides.storyContext: The frog reached the sky because he believed. He jumped when others doubted. He rose when he fell. You can do the same.

image.alt: The Frog's Gift — The Frog

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Obstacle (barrier), determination (never-give-up spirit), courage (bravery), exhausted (very tired), renewed (given new energy).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: obstacle, determination, courage, exhausted, renewed, strength

image.alt: New Words Learned — The Frog

subject: English
title: Gilli Danda: A Village Game
hook: An ancient Indian game teaches friendship, skill, and the joy of playing outdoors together.

slides.title: An Old Game in a Village
slides.storyContext: In a small village, children gather at sunset with two wooden sticks. Arjun watches as Ravi teaches him gilli danda, a game played for centuries.
slides.inSimpleWords: Ancient games connect us to history.

image.alt: An Old Game in a Village — Gilli Danda

slides.title: What is Gilli Danda?
slides.storyContext: Ravi explains: 'The gilli is a small stick, the danda is bigger. You tap the gilli to make it fly, then hit it far. Try to run and win!'

points.label: The game
points.text: A bat-and-stick game with roots in Indian villages for over 2,500 years

points.label: The rules
points.text: Tap the stick to flip it, then hit it as far as you can. Run and return before others catch you

slides.inSimpleWords: Gilli danda is skill and speed.

image.alt: What is Gilli Danda? — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Arjun's First Try
slides.storyContext: Arjun grips the danda nervously. He taps the gilli. It flies! He swings hard and hits it far across the field. He laughs with joy.

image.alt: Arjun's First Try — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Teamwork and Strategy
slides.storyContext: Ravi teaches: 'Watch your opponent. Learn where they hit. Play as a team. The player who hits farthest and returns safely wins.'

example.problem: How do you win at gilli danda?
example.solution: Skill (hitting far), speed (running fast), and strategy (reading the game)

image.alt: Teamwork and Strategy — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Why This Game Matters
slides.storyContext: As the sun sets, Ravi tells Arjun: 'This game connects us to our grandparents and their grandparents. It's part of who we are as Indians.'

points.label: Cultural treasure
points.text: Gilli danda is part of Indian heritage, played across villages for millennia

points.label: Life lesson
points.text: Sometimes the simplest games teach the deepest lessons about courage, skill, and community

image.alt: Why This Game Matters — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Play and Learn
slides.storyContext: Arjun challenges his friends to play. They form teams. They laugh. They celebrate. They build memories under the village sky.

points.label: Your turn
points.text: Learn gilli danda or another traditional game. Play with friends. Feel the connection to your heritage

image.alt: Play and Learn — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Sunset Wisdom
slides.storyContext: As the game ends, Ravi and Arjun sit together. They realize: the game isn't just about winning. It's about playing together, laughing, and making memories.
slides.inSimpleWords: Games are about joy, not just winning.

image.alt: Sunset Wisdom — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Gilli Danda Teaches Us
slides.storyContext: A simple game with two sticks teaches skill, courage, strategy, and community. It reminds us that the best treasures are time with friends.

image.alt: Gilli Danda Teaches Us — Gilli Danda

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Gilli (small stick), danda (larger stick), heritage (cultural inheritance), strategy (game plan), traditional (passed down through time).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: gilli, danda, heritage, tradition, strategy, community

image.alt: New Words Learned — Gilli Danda

subject: English
title: The Raven and the Fox: A Fable of Flattery
hook: A vain raven learns a bitter lesson when a cunning fox uses flattery to steal his cheese.

slides.title: The Prize Cheese
slides.storyContext: A raven sits on a high branch with a piece of cheese in his beak. Below, a hungry fox looks up and smiles slyly. 'What a beautiful raven,' she thinks.

image.alt: The Prize Cheese — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Fox's Plan
slides.storyContext: The fox approaches sweetly: 'Dear Raven, I've heard your voice is the most beautiful of all birds. Would you sing for me?'

image.alt: The Fox's Plan — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: Pride and Vanity
slides.storyContext: The raven's chest swells with pride. He has always wished to be recognized for his beauty and his voice. The fox's words touch his heart.

points.label: What is vanity?
points.text: Excessive pride in one's appearance, abilities, or importance

points.label: The danger
points.text: Vanity makes us believe false compliments and blind us to deception

image.alt: Pride and Vanity — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Raven Opens His Beak
slides.storyContext: Unable to resist, the raven opens his beak to sing. The cheese falls! The fox catches it and laughs: 'You've been fooled, foolish bird!'

example.problem: Why did the raven fall for such an obvious trick?
example.solution: Because vanity wants to believe compliments, even when they seem too good to be true

slides.inSimpleWords: Vanity leads to our own downfall.

image.alt: The Raven Opens His Beak — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Lesson of Flattery
slides.storyContext: The raven realizes too late: the fox didn't care about his voice. She only wanted the cheese. Her words were tricks, not truth.

points.label: About flattery
points.text: False praise often hides bad intentions. Real friends admire you, but don't ask you to sacrifice things

points.label: The moral
points.text: Be wise. Question compliments that ask you to do strange things. A true friend never manipulates you

image.alt: The Lesson of Flattery — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: Spot the Flattery
slides.storyContext: Someone says: 'You're so smart, you could break that school rule without consequence!' How would you respond?

points.label: The answer
points.text: Recognize the flattery. Refuse the trap. Real friends don't ask you to do wrong things

slides.inSimpleWords: Guard against flattery in real life.

image.alt: Spot the Flattery — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Raven's Wisdom
slides.storyContext: The raven sits alone, sad and wiser. He learns: kindness matters more than compliments. Humility protects better than pride.

image.alt: The Raven's Wisdom — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Fable's Gift
slides.storyContext: The raven and fox teach us: vanity blinds us. Flattery can deceive us. The answer is humility and wisdom.
slides.inSimpleWords: Be humble. Be wise. Be safe.

image.alt: The Fable's Gift — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Vanity (excessive pride), flattery (false praise), deception (trickery), humility (modesty), slyly (cleverly and sneakily).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: vanity, flattery, deception, humility, sly, manipulate

image.alt: New Words Learned — The Raven and the Fox

subject: English
title: Rama to the Rescue: Courage and Duty
hook: From the Ramayana, Rama's journey teaches us about duty, courage, and the triumph of good over evil.

slides.title: Sita Is Taken
slides.storyContext: The evil Ravana captures Princess Sita and takes her across the ocean to his island kingdom of Lanka. Rama learns of her suffering and swears to rescue her.
slides.inSimpleWords: Even heroes face their darkest tests.

image.alt: Sita Is Taken — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: The Journey Begins
slides.storyContext: Rama and his loyal brother Lakshmana, joined by the brave monkey king Hanuman, begin a dangerous journey across mountains and oceans.
slides.inSimpleWords: True friends stand with you always.

image.alt: The Journey Begins — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: Duty Over Comfort
slides.storyContext: Rama could have stayed in his palace, safe and comfortable. Instead, he chose duty: to save Sita and protect dharma (righteousness).

points.label: Rama's choice
points.text: He left comfort, family, and safety to fulfill his duty

points.label: The lesson
points.text: True courage means doing what is right, even when it is hard and dangerous

image.alt: Duty Over Comfort — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: Hanuman's Loyalty
slides.storyContext: Hanuman, Rama's devoted follower, offers his service: 'I will cross the ocean alone to find Sita and bring news to you.' He loves Rama with all his heart.

example.problem: How do we show loyalty to those we love?
example.solution: By standing with them, helping them, and never abandoning them in times of need

image.alt: Hanuman's Loyalty — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: The Battle for Dharma
slides.storyContext: Rama and Ravana clash in a final battle. Rama fights not from anger, but from duty. He defeats evil and rescues Sita, restoring righteousness.

points.label: Good vs. evil
points.text: Rama represents dharma (righteousness), Ravana represents adharma (unrighteousness)

points.label: The truth
points.text: Good will always triumph over evil, but it requires courage, sacrifice, and unwavering truth

image.alt: The Battle for Dharma — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: What Would You Do?
slides.storyContext: If someone you loved was in danger far away, would you risk everything to rescue them? What sacrifices would you make?

points.label: Your answer
points.text: Think about the people you love and the duties you have toward them

slides.inSimpleWords: Love and duty shape who we are.

image.alt: What Would You Do? — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: Sita's Return
slides.storyContext: Sita is found and rescued! But Rama's duty extends beyond: he must rule justly and protect his kingdom for all his people.

image.alt: Sita's Return — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: Rama's Legacy
slides.storyContext: Rama teaches: courage faces evil. Duty binds us to those we love. Righteousness triumphs. These are truths that echo through millennia.
slides.inSimpleWords: Rama shows us how to live truly.

image.alt: Rama's Legacy — Rama to the Rescue

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Dharma (righteousness), adharma (unrighteousness), loyalty (faithful devotion), sacrifice (giving up for others), triumph (victory).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: dharma, adharma, loyalty, duty, sacrifice, triumph, righteousness

image.alt: New Words Learned — Rama to the Rescue

subject: English
title: The Unlikely Best Friends: Friendship Beyond Differences
hook: A lion and a mouse prove that true friendship knows no size, strength, or difference. Together, they're unstoppable.

slides.title: An Unlikely Meeting
slides.storyContext: A tiny mouse stumbles into a lion's den. The lion could crush him with one paw. Instead, the mouse looks up bravely and says: 'Please don't hurt me.'

image.alt: An Unlikely Meeting — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: The Mouse's Promise
slides.storyContext: The lion smiles and lets the mouse go free. The mouse bows and promises: 'Someday, I will repay your kindness.' The lion laughs at such a small promise.

image.alt: The Mouse's Promise — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: Friendship Without Judgment
slides.storyContext: The lion and mouse become friends. The lion doesn't look down on the mouse for being small. The mouse doesn't fear the lion for being strong. They see each other's hearts.

points.label: True friendship
points.text: Doesn't judge by size, strength, wealth, or appearance

points.label: The lesson
points.text: Real friends value character and kindness, not external differences

image.alt: Friendship Without Judgment — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: The Rescue
slides.storyContext: One day, hunters capture the lion in a net. He roars in anger and fear. The mouse appears and gnaws through the ropes with tiny but determined teeth.

example.problem: How can a tiny mouse help a mighty lion?
example.solution: Through courage, determination, and the fact that friendship isn't about size—it's about heart

slides.inSimpleWords: Small acts of courage matter most.

image.alt: The Rescue — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: The Power of Helping Others
slides.storyContext: The lion is free! He realizes: the mouse kept his promise. A small friend with a big heart is worth more than a thousand powerful enemies.

points.label: The wisdom
points.text: Never underestimate anyone. Never assume you can't make a difference

points.label: About gratitude
points.text: True friends remember kindness and return it, no matter the cost

image.alt: The Power of Helping Others — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: Find Your Unlikely Friend
slides.storyContext: Is there someone very different from you whom you could befriend? What differences do you notice? What similarities do you share?

points.label: Your reflection
points.text: The best friendships often cross boundaries of age, background, ability, and belief

image.alt: Find Your Unlikely Friend — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: Friends Forever
slides.storyContext: The lion and mouse walk together through the forest. The lion tall and strong, the mouse small but brave. They need each other. They complete each other.

image.alt: Friends Forever — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: The Fable's Truth
slides.storyContext: Size doesn't matter. Strength doesn't matter. What matters is kindness, loyalty, courage, and the choice to see the best in others.
slides.inSimpleWords: All hearts are equal in friendship.

image.alt: The Fable's Truth — The Unlikely Best Friends

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Unlikely (surprising), determined (fixed in purpose), gratitude (thankfulness), character (moral qualities), loyalty (faithfulness).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: unlikely, determined, gratitude, character, loyalty, kindness

image.alt: New Words Learned — The Unlikely Best Friends

subject: English
title: What a Bird Thought: A Gentle Poem of Perspective
hook: Through a bird's eyes, we see that the world we know is vast and mysterious to those who see it differently.

slides.title: The Bird's Window
slides.storyContext: A small bird perches on a child's window. It watches the world of rooms and houses below. To the bird, human spaces are as strange as clouds are to us.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every creature sees the world differently.

image.alt: The Bird's Window — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: What Does the Bird Think?
slides.storyContext: The bird wonders: What are these glass barriers? Why don't humans fly? Why do they stay in boxes? To the bird, humans are the curious creatures.

points.label: Perspective shift
points.text: Things we think are normal seem strange to others who see them differently

points.label: The learning
points.text: Understanding how others view our world teaches us humility and empathy

image.alt: What Does the Bird Think? — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: The Bird's Freedom
slides.storyContext: The bird flies away, soaring above the houses. The child watches from the window. Each sees the other as unable to understand their world.
slides.inSimpleWords: Freedom looks different to different beings.

image.alt: The Bird's Freedom — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: What the Bird Knows
slides.storyContext: The bird knows the vastness of the sky, the joy of wind under wings, the loneliness of migration. These are truths the child might never fully understand.

example.problem: How do we understand things so different from us?
example.solution: Through imagination, kindness, and respect for ways of life unlike our own

image.alt: What the Bird Knows — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: The Poem's Deeper Meaning
slides.storyContext: The poem teaches: we are all creatures in a vast world. What seems normal to us is strange to others. Every perspective is valid.

points.label: About empathy
points.text: To understand someone, try to see the world through their eyes

points.label: The beauty
points.text: Diversity of perspective makes the world richer, not more confusing

image.alt: The Poem's Deeper Meaning — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: See Through Another's Eyes
slides.storyContext: Choose an animal: a dog, fish, or ant. What might they think about human life? How might their day look from their perspective?

points.label: Try this
points.text: Write or draw what a dog might think about your daily life. How strange might it seem to them?

image.alt: See Through Another's Eyes — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: Connection Across Worlds
slides.storyContext: The bird flies back to the window. The child smiles. For a moment, their eyes meet. Two worlds touch, and each wonders about the other.

image.alt: Connection Across Worlds — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: The Lesson of Perspective
slides.storyContext: What a bird thinks teaches us: the world is vast. Perspectives vary. Kindness means honoring all ways of seeing and being.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every viewpoint has value and beauty.

image.alt: The Lesson of Perspective — What a Bird Thought

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Perspective (way of seeing), empathy (understanding others' feelings), migrant (one who travels), vast (very large), validity (truth or worth).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: perspective, empathy, vast, wonder, diverse, perception

image.alt: New Words Learned — What a Bird Thought
